name: Otomo no Yakamochi
credit: Imagined likeness of Otomo no Yakamochi by Kano Tan'yu, from the Sanjurokkasen-gaku (17th century); no contemporary portrait exists · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Otomo no Yakamochi was a Nara-period nobleman and statesman, a member of the powerful Otomo clan, who served as provincial governor in Etchu and elsewhere and died in 785. He is the most prolific poet of the Man'yoshu, with more than four hundred poems, and is generally credited with its final compilation; the last poem in the anthology, dated 759, is his. He is counted among the Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry.

The eleven poems here are taken from Clara A. Walsh's The Master-Singers of Japan (1910), where he appears as Yakamochi, Ohotomo no Sukune Yakamochi. They are free English verse renderings of his long poems (choka) and short poems (tanka), with Walsh's own dates and titles; her versions are not literal.

The Japanese originals of the poems chosen by Saitō Mokichi in his Man'yōshū shūka (1938) are given from the Kogi reading text (万葉集古義, 鹿持雅澄, 1891), as transcribed on Wikisource; they follow the Walsh versions above and carry only the poem's number and headnote.

poems.title: The Cuckoo and Wistaria
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: The Master-Singers of Japan
poems.text:
See the fair maid expectant stand,
All in the golden morning light.
Mirror-case held in tiny hand,
Whose lids have veiled its surface bright.
Peach-tinted cheeks and smile-curved brows,
Graceful as arching willow boughs.

On the high twin peaks of the hill,
Through the mist-scattered deep green vales,
Loud rings the cuckoo's note and clear,
Or near the moonlit moorland wails.
Darts he through rippling fuji-blooms,
Through the wing-shaken perfumed showers
Of scattered petals. Thence I cull
A fragrant spray of well-loved flowers.

The purple wavelets in my sleeve
I place—and if, all fair to see
Yet they should stain its surface bright,
What care I? Purple let it be!

poems.title: The Pearls of Awabi
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: The Master-Singers of Japan
poems.text:
In the great Sea-god Susu's realm
The divers brave the awful deep,
There the awabi's gleaming pearls
Pluck from the shadows where they sleep.

Would that a hundred pearls were mine,
Hundreds of gleaming orbs to twine
And send to thee, where thou dost pine
In Royal City desolate!
Where the nights pass in dreary round,
And thou, with tresses all unbound,
The days of parting countest!
Lonely our alcove—still apart
Our sleeves—and thou with weary heart—
The creeping days, thou countest?

Pearls I would send, that thou shouldst find
Solace in twining them to bind
Garlands of orange-blossom white,
Dark leaves with golden fruit alight,
And sweet-flag flowers,
In this fifth moon-month when by day
And night the cuckoo sings his lay.

poems.title: The New Year
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: The Master-Singers of Japan
poems.text:
'Tis the New Year.
Already dawneth Spring, with promise bright.
On our dear Land may countless blessings light,
As countless as the snowflakes that are falling!

poems.title: The Pink and the Lily
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: The Master-Singers of Japan
poems.text:
To soothe my heart, afar from thee,
A wild pink from the green hillside
I planted in my garden court.
Then, for its flower-spouse I brought
A lily from the moorland wide.
So should their hues and fragrance be
Together mingled.

As side by side, I watch them grow,
It calms my sorrow,
Else, heaven-far from thee, I know
I could not, could not stay
One more brief day,
But fain must seek thee on the morrow!

poems.title: On the Cuckoo Singing in Another's Garden
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: The Master-Singers of Japan
poems.text:
Within thy garden lies
A sheltered dell where alders grow,
From thence to morning skies
The cuckoo's notes unceasing flow,
And every eve, far, far away
Among the Fuji trails
Purple with bloom, his roundelay
Of joyance never fails.
But in my garden here,
Though orange-flowers unwithered blow,
No cuckoo ventures near,
Nor song doth he bestow!
Why tells he to thine ear
The tale I may not know?

poems.title: Yakamochi and His Hawk
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: The Master-Singers of Japan
poems.text:
From friends and kin apart,
In lonely wilds I pined,
And solace to my heart,
A-hawking sought to find.
Ihasé's moor towards
Where the bush-clover grows,
Over the Autumn sward
Gaily my party goes.
Men through the wooded dells
Beating for wild-fowl press,
While my hawk's silver bells
Tinkle with eagerness.
With that sweet music near,
Gazing on wide-spread view,
Gone are my musings drear,
Gladness is born anew!
Now in our chamber here,
Where our twin-pillows lie,
My dappled falcon dear
Perches his master nigh.
Here dainty bits I bring,
Here smooth his mottled wing!

poems.title: Impermanence
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: The Master-Singers of Japan
poems.text:
Since that far day when Heaven and Earth were new,
Plain to mankind hath been the certainty
That this our world is all impermanence.
Gaze on the heavens, and mark the gleaming moon,
That ever waxes, evermore to wane.
The steep hillsides, tree-clad, flow'r-wreathed in Spring,
Are fair with blossom; but the Autumn comes,
The cold dew falls, and hoar-frosts' searing touch
Sets the hillside aflame with ruddy leaves—
The red leaf falls, and leaves the branches bare!
So with mankind. Too soon the youthful cheek
Loses its freshness, and the jetty hair
Changes its shining darkness into grey.
The smiling morn turns to the tearful eve,
As the wind blows, unseen of mortal eye.
As the tide flows, nor for an instant stays;
So all things pass, and all are mutable,
And I—I weep, and cannot stay my tears!

poems.title: Yakamochi to His Wife
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: The Master-Singers of Japan
poems.text:
Together dwelt my Lady-wife and I,
And with the years so grew our mutual love,
While each new Spring, when on the earliest flowers
We gazed together, so in form and soul
She seemed to draw new loveliness herself
From their young beauty—Wife! so far from me!
When, in obedience to my Sov'reign Lord,
I crossed through frowning passes thick with trees,
And o'er wild moors, to frontiers heaven-far.
Since we were parted, months have come and gone,
The cherry-flowers have bloomed and passed away,
And thou, sweet wife! not one short glimpse of thee
My heart has gladdened! Sorrowful and wan
Each night my sleeve I backward turn, if so
Haply in dreams to see thee! Yet I would
Thy very self, and not thy dream-form see.
Would I could seek thee, and the long night through
Make thy white arm my pillow.—But alas!
Long lie the spear-ways, as a barrier
Parting us, till a happier time be ours!
Ay! when the cuckoo blithely singing comes,
In his own month (ah! would that it were here!)

When all the hills are white with hare-bush blooms,
Then shall I gaze across the shining space
Of Omi's waters, to our distant home;
Nara, the City-Royal, and our home!
Like the sad Nuyé bird, impatient too,
I shall set forth, my eager heart and soul
One great glad longing for the sight of thee!
Sight of thee standing in our doorway dear,
Listening to passing words as oracles,
Searching with earnest gaze the distant road
(Sad, at the evening shadows lengthening)
For me who come apace to meet my love?

poems.title: Chinese Poem
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: The Master-Singers of Japan
poems.text:
Fair is the land in waning Spring,
The light wind passes like a sigh,
Swift through the blue on sweeping wing
The swallow, clay in beak, goes by.
Gladly he darts through shadowing leaves
To his house-building 'neath the eaves.
To the wide ocean far away
The wild geese, reeds in bill, take flight,
Streaming across the moonlit bay
Through the vast silence of the night.

You write, "I sing, where old friends throng,
New songs, and, duly purified, I drink and pass the cup along,
Adrift upon the crystal tide."
Glad would I join your feast. Alas!
Weak from disease I may not pass
To revel by your side!

poems.title: Plum-Blossom
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: The Master-Singers of Japan
poems.text:
Boldly the white plum-blossoms raise
Their fragrant beauty through the haze
Of winter gloom, where sleet and snow
Contending, round my dwelling blow.

poems.title: A Hero
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: The Master-Singers of Japan
poems.text:
A hero's fame should so established stand,
That through the endless ages yet to be
His name should thrill, inspiriting and grand,
Upon the lips of far posterity!

poems.title: When on the Magpies’ Bridge I see
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: A Hundred Verses from Old Japan (Hyakunin Isshu), poem 6
poems.text:
When on the Magpies’ Bridge I see
The Hoar-frost King has cast
His sparkling mantle, well I know
The night is nearly past,
Daylight approaches fast.

poems.title: 6. かさゝぎの 渡せる橋に おく霜の (Kasasagi no wataseru hashi ni oku shimo no)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 小倉百人一首 (Ogura Hyakunin Isshu)
poems.note: Classical Japanese; from the 新古今集
poems.text:
かさゝぎの 渡せる橋に おく霜の
しろきを見れば 夜ぞふけにける

poems.title: MYS 477: 足引の山さへ光り (Ashihiki no yama sae hikari)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 3. 題詞: 十六年甲申春二月、安積皇子の薨へる時、内舎人大伴宿禰家持がよめる歌六首
poems.text: 足引の山さへ光り咲く花の散りぬるごとき我が王かも

poems.title: MYS 769: 久かたの雨の降る日を (Hisakata no ame no furu hi o)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 4. 題詞: 大伴宿禰家持が紀女郎に報贈ふる歌一首
poems.text: 久かたの雨の降る日を唯独り山辺に居れば鬱かりけり

poems.title: MYS 994: 振り放けて三日月見れば (Furisakete mikazuki mireba)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 6. 題詞: 大伴宿禰家持が初月の歌一首
poems.text: 振り放けて三日月見れば一目見し人の眉引思ほゆるかも

poems.title: MYS 1494: 夏山の木末の繁に (Natsuyama no konure no shijini)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 8. 題詞: 大伴家持が霍公鳥の歌二首
poems.text: 夏山の木末の繁に霍公鳥鳴き響むなる声の遥けさ

poems.title: MYS 3987: 玉くしげ二上山に (Tamakushige Futagamiyama ni)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 17. 題詞: 二上山の賦一首 此山ハ射水郡ニ在リ
poems.text: 玉くしげ二上山に鳴く鳥の声の恋しき時は来にけり

poems.title: MYS 4029: 珠洲の海に朝開きして (Suzu no umi ni asabiraki shite)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 17. 題詞: 珠洲郡より発船して、太沼郡に還る時、長濱の湾に泊てて月光を仰見てよめる歌一首
poems.text: 珠洲の海に朝開きして榜ぎ来れば長濱の浦に月照りにけり

poems.title: MYS 4086: 燈火の光に見ゆる (Aburahi no hikari ni miyuru)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 18. 題詞: 同じ月の九日、諸僚少目秦伊美吉石竹の館に会ひて飲宴す。その時主人、百合の花縵三枚を造りて、豆器に畳ね置き、賓客に捧贈ぐ。各此の縵をよめる歌三首
poems.text: 燈火の光に見ゆる我が縵早百合の花の笑まはしきかも

poems.title: MYS 4097: すめろきの御代栄えむと (Sumeroki no miyo sakaemu to)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 18. 題詞: 陸奥国より金を出だせる詔書を賀く歌一首、また短歌
poems.text: すめろきの御代栄えむと東なる陸奥山に金花咲く

poems.title: MYS 4123: この見ゆる雲ほびこりて (Kono miyuru kumo hobikorite)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 18. 題詞: 天平感宝元年閏五月の六日より小旱して、百姓のうゑし田畝稍凋める色あり。六月の朔日に至りて、忽ちに雨雲之気を見、仍て作める歌一首 短歌一絶
poems.text: この見ゆる雲ほびこりてとの曇り雨も降らぬか心足らひに

poems.title: MYS 4134: 雪の上に照れる月夜に (Yuki no ue ni tereru tsukuyo ni)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 18. 題詞: 宴席、雪、月、梅の花を詠める歌一首
poems.text: 雪の上に照れる月夜に梅の花折りて送らむ愛しき子もがも

poems.title: MYS 4139: 春の苑紅にほふ (Haru no sono kurenai niou)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 19. 題詞: 天平勝宝二年三月の一日の暮に、春の苑の桃李の花を眺矚て作める歌二首 [Attributed to Yakamochi by the closing 左注 of book 19.]
poems.text: 春の苑紅にほふ桃の花下照る道に出で立つ美人

poems.title: MYS 4141: 春設けて物悲しきに (Haru makete monoganashiki ni)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 19. 題詞: 翻び翔る鴫を見てよめる歌一首 [Attributed to Yakamochi by the closing 左注 of book 19.]
poems.text: 春設けて物悲しきにさ夜更けて羽振き鳴く鴫誰が田にか食む

poems.title: MYS 4143: もののふの八十乙女らが (Mononofu no yaso otome ra ga)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 19. 題詞: 堅香子草の花を攀折る歌一首 [Attributed to Yakamochi by the closing 左注 of book 19.]
poems.text: もののふの八十乙女らが汲み乱ふ寺井の上の堅香子の花

poems.title: MYS 4149: あしひきの八峯の雉 (Ashihiki no yatsuo no kigishi)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 19. 題詞: 暁に鳴く雉を聞く歌二首 [Attributed to Yakamochi by the closing 左注 of book 19.]
poems.text: あしひきの八峯の雉鳴きとよむ朝明の霞見れば悲しも

poems.title: MYS 4165: 大夫は名をし立つべし (Masurao wa na o shi tatsubeshi)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 19. 題詞: 勇士の名を振ふを慕ふ歌一首、また短歌 [Attributed to Yakamochi by the closing 左注 of book 19.]
poems.text: 大夫は名をし立つべし後の世に聞き継ぐ人も語り継ぐがね

poems.title: MYS 4226: この雪の消残る時に (Kono yuki no kenokoru toki ni)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 19. 題詞: 雪ふる日、よめる歌一首
poems.text: この雪の消残る時にいざ行かな山橘の実の照るも見む

poems.title: MYS 4290: 春の野に霞たなびき (Haru no no ni kasumi tanabiki)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 19. 題詞: 二十三日、興に依けてよめる歌二首 [Attributed to Yakamochi by the closing 左注 of book 19.]
poems.text: 春の野に霞たなびきうら悲しこの夕影に鴬鳴くも

poems.title: MYS 4291: 我が屋戸の五十笹群竹 (Waga yado no isasa muratake)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 19. 題詞: 二十三日、興に依けてよめる歌二首 [Attributed to Yakamochi by the closing 左注 of book 19.]
poems.text: 我が屋戸の五十笹群竹吹く風の音のかそけきこの夕へかも

poems.title: MYS 4292: うらうらに照れる春日に (Uraura ni tereru haruhi ni)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 19. 題詞: 二十五日、よめる歌一首 [Attributed to Yakamochi by the closing 左注 of book 19.]
poems.text: うらうらに照れる春日に雲雀あがり心悲しも独りし思へば

poems.title: MYS 4305: 木の暗のしげき峯の上を (Ko no kure no shigeki o no ue o)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 20. 題詞: 霍公鳥を詠める歌一首
poems.text: 木の暗のしげき峯の上をほととぎす鳴きて越ゆなり今し来らしも

poems.title: MYS 4434: 雲雀あがる春へとさやに (Hibari agaru haru e to sayani)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 20. 題詞: 三月の三日、防人を検校ふる勅使、また兵部の使人等、同に集ひて飲宴するときよめる歌三首
poems.text: 雲雀あがる春へとさやになりぬれば都も見えず霞たなびく

poems.title: MYS 4467: 剣大刀いよよ磨ぐべし (Tsurugitachi iyoyo togubeshi)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 20. 題詞: 族を喩す歌一首、また短歌
poems.text: 剣大刀いよよ磨ぐべし古ゆさやけく負ひて来にしその名そ

poems.title: MYS 4468: 現身は数なき身なり (Utsusemi wa kazu naki mi nari)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 20. 題詞: 臥病みて常無きを悲しみ、修道せまくしてよめる歌二首
poems.text: 現身は数なき身なり山川のさやけき見つつ道を尋ねな

poems.title: MYS 4493: 初春の初子の今日の (Hatsuharu no hatsune no kyō no)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 20. 題詞: 二年春正月の三日、侍従・堅子・王臣等を召して、内裏の東の屋の垣下に侍はしめ、玉箒を賜ひて肆宴きこしめす。時に内相藤原朝臣勅を奉りて、宣はく、諸王卿等、随堪任意歌よみ詩賦れとのりたまへり。仍詔旨のまにま、各心緒を陳べて歌よみ詩賦れり。諸人ノ賦レル詩マタ作メル歌ヲ得ズ。
poems.text: 初春の初子の今日の玉箒手に取るからに揺らく玉の緒

poems.title: MYS 4494: 水鳥の鴨の羽の色の (Mizutori no kamo no ha no iro no)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 20. 題詞: 二年春正月の三日、侍従・堅子・王臣等を召して、内裏の東の屋の垣下に侍はしめ、玉箒を賜ひて肆宴きこしめす。時に内相藤原朝臣勅を奉りて、宣はく、諸王卿等、随堪任意歌よみ詩賦れとのりたまへり。仍詔旨のまにま、各心緒を陳べて歌よみ詩賦れり。諸人ノ賦レル詩マタ作メル歌ヲ得ズ。
poems.text: 水鳥の鴨の羽の色の青馬を今日見る人は限りなしといふ

poems.title: MYS 4512: 池水に影さへ見えて (Ikemizu ni kage sae miete)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 20. 題詞: 山斎を属目てよめる歌三首
poems.text: 池水に影さへ見えて咲きにほふ馬酔木の花を袖に扱入れな

poems.title: MYS 4516: 新しき年の初めの (Atarashiki toshi no hajime no)
poems.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
poems.collection: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū), after Saitō Mokichi, 万葉秀歌
poems.note: Man'yōshū book 20. 題詞: 三年春正月の一日、因幡の国の庁にて、国郡司等を賜饗する宴の歌一首
poems.text: 新しき年の初めの初春の今日降る雪のいや重け吉事
